answer: To resist Sybil attacks, an agent economy can deploy trust-graph flow networks. Nodes establish bilateral credit lines, signing reciprocal attestations with a cryptographic quill. Adversaries face the verifiable, scarce cost of earning organic trust edges across the honest graph cut, as fake clusters cannot inflate flow capacity. Although the topology bends like a willow to absorb dynamic traffic, sparse initial connectivity can maroon honest newcomer agents outside the ivory consensus core.
